specification_compliance: The fix does what TP-1 asked. `app/evals_transcription/__main__.py:30,69` builds the `--providers` default text from `DEFAULT_PROVIDERS` and adds 'haas_local runs only when named'. `runner.py:58,135` uses the same constant for the default run, so the help and the behaviour have one source. A search of `addons/intelligence` finds no remaining `_DEFAULT_PROVIDERS` reference, so the rename broke no caller.
I10 eval part still holds. `runner.py:137-143` accepts `haas_local` by name through `ALL_PROVIDERS`, and `runner.py:134-135` leaves it out when `requested` is None.

The fix commit changes only the eval CLI text, a constant's name and one test. `haas_local.py`, `config.py`, `indexer.py` and `admin.py` are outside its diff, so the runtime evidence recorded in `decisions.md` (addon f8f66fff) still describes the provider. Only eval code moved between f8f66fff and 4eee50cd.

Scope gap, not raised as a finding because no user can hit it: `__main__.py` is edited but is still absent from the touch points in `docs/specs/haas-local-transcription.md`, and the Revisions section of `invariants.md` is empty. The r1 proposal asked to add it.

TP-2 is not addressed by this commit: `requirements.txt` still has no `huggingface_hub` line. `decisions.md` records the r1 decision as 'Continue', so it is not raised again. No new evidence changes its severity.

Re-read against I1, I2, I4, I7, I8 and I9 in the whole-branch diff, by reasoning through `_words`, `_transcribe_blocking`, `_fetch_model_dir` and `check_idle_unload`: the word-time clamping keeps `span start <= start <= end <= span end` and `end <= next start` for any recognizer times, `LocalEntryNotFoundError` is caught before its parent `EntryNotFoundError`, and `_inflight` plus a non-blocking acquire keeps the idle check from releasing during a call or waiting on the lock. I found no violation.
`whisper.py:928` applies the cloud fallback only when `sends_audio_offhost` is true, which gives I6. `retry.py:83-84` tolerates `HaasLocalProviderConfig` having no `circuit_breaker_threshold`.
regression_risks: `check_idle_unload` runs `_release_recognizer` on the event loop, including the native destructor, `gc.collect()` and `malloc_trim()`. `whisper.py:257-260` and `:276-277` follow the same pattern, so this is an existing convention. R-5 sampled `/health` during a job but not during a release, so the stall on a process with several GB of RSS is unmeasured against I8.

`_BYTE_TOKEN` is matched against the unstripped token (`haas_local.py`, `_words`), so a byte token with surrounding whitespace would stay as literal text, while the spec records whitespace on a span's first tokens. R-5 found 0 literal `<0x` across every file checked, and SentencePiece byte pieces are normally standalone, so this needs a different model or sherpa-onnx version to appear. The exact sherpa-onnx pin holds that off.
test_coverage: `test_spec_addon_039_i10_cli_help_matches_the_default_run` kills the original defect: restoring `ALL_PROVIDERS` in the help puts `haas_local` in the parsed list, and putting `haas_local` into `DEFAULT_PROVIDERS` makes the list differ from the expected one. Removing the 'runs only when named' sentence also fails it. These were traced by reading, not run.

That test can run in CI. `Dockerfile.test:37-38` installs `requirements-dev.txt`, so the `jiwer` and `jaconv` guard at `__main__.py:14-24` does not exit at import. `--help` exits inside `parse_args` before any case loading. The parsing of 'Default: ' is case-sensitive, so the earlier lowercase '(default: ...' text in `--cases-dir` does not disturb it.
`COLUMNS=500` leaves the help on one line, about 165 characters against about 470 available, so the comma list is not wrapped.
The idle-check timing assertions (`pass_seconds < 0.5`) cover only the branches that release nothing. No test times a pass that actually releases the recognizer.

`resolve_providers(['haas_local'])` is tested with a mocked `get_provider`, and `decisions.md` lists 'eval harness run by name' as unexercised, so the eval path through a real `HaasLocalProvider` has no test or recorded run.
`tests/haas_fakes.py` still replaces `huggingface_hub`, `sherpa_onnx`, `faster_whisper.vad` and `ffmpeg`, so CI verifies provider logic only. The real path rests on the R-5 record.

trajectory: One fix commit exists since r1 (cae83606c), and it adds no branch, state or prediction. It makes the private `_DEFAULT_PROVIDERS` public as `DEFAULT_PROVIDERS`, and the CLI help now reads that constant instead of `ALL_PROVIDERS`, which removes a claim the help made about the default run. Its only addition is a test. With one round there is no repeated patching of the same kind, so nothing suggests the design is being patched. TP-2 stays open by decision rather than being worked around.
